title: Floor Patterns: Herringbone, Chevron, Straight and Wide Plank
description: One hall, four hardwood floor patterns: herringbone, chevron, straight and wide plank, with what to check and ask before you choose a layout.
dek: Same walls, door and window. Only the floor pattern changes. Compare four on screen, then plan the layout on your own floor.
hook: A pattern name on a sample card is hard to picture across a whole room. This guide shows one hall with the same walls, six-panel door, window and baseboards over four floor patterns, so the layout is the only thing that changes.

The images are AI-generated concept pictures, not photos of a real floor. The board sizes and the wood tone are for comparison only, not a product. A real floor depends on the board size, the room shape and how your installer lays it out.
gallery_intro: Straight plank and wide plank run in one direction. Herringbone zigzags with square-ended blocks. Chevron meets angled planks in a continuous V. Walls, door, window and baseboards stay the same in every look.

tips.p: Patterns draw the eye. In a large open room a pattern can be the feature. In a small or busy room, straight or wide plank tends to feel calmer. Picture the rugs and furniture that will cover part of the floor.

With straight boards, installers often suggest running them along the longest wall or toward the main light. Ask yours which suits your room, and ask how the floor will meet the next room at the doorway.

Herringbone uses square-ended blocks laid at right angles, so the zigzag steps at each block. Chevron cuts the board ends at an angle so the V lines run unbroken. Chevron tends to look sharper, and herringbone tends to look more textured.

A pattern usually takes more cutting and fitting than straight boards. Ask your installer about extra material and extra labor before you compare quotes, and ask how the pattern will end at walls and doorways.
A pattern can show uneven spots and gaps more than straight boards do. Ask your installer to check that the subfloor is flat, and to explain where the layout will start.

tips.h: Check the product and the wood
tips.p: Not every product comes in every pattern, and chevron is often sold as matched left and right pieces. Wider boards can move more with humidity. Read the maker's install guide, and ask whether solid or engineered wood suits your room.

final: If you do one thing, ask to see a few boards laid out in the pattern, and look at them from the doorway in your own light. A pattern that looks calm on a screen can feel busy across a real room.
